# Implementation Accelerator Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Implementation Accelerator, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client describes its AI maturity as piloting. It has three AI use cases at different lifecycle stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Three facts from the Profile Block shape this proposal:

- An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.
- The Client has named the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers.
- The Client intends to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, although the start date is not fixed.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Client has also set three constraints:

- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## 2. Why an Intensive AIMS Foundation Build Fits

**Decision timeline.** A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. Your stated objective points to Q2 2027 as the period in which visual inspection is expected to go into production. A five-day intensive produces a working set of governance artifacts in one concentrated week. This leaves the Client with time after the Accelerator to review the artifacts, adopt them and begin operating them before Q2 2027. The exact time available depends on the Accelerator dates, which are Unknown until the Client confirms them.

**Certification targets.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year. The artifacts built in the Accelerator are structured for future conformity work against ISO/IEC 42001. The aim is readiness, so that the Client starts that work with a charter, inventory, risk register, policy set and evidence model already drafted. The Accelerator does not promise ISO/IEC 42001 certification or any audit outcome.

**Audit finding.** The June 2026 internal audit finding concerns the absence of an AI system inventory. Day 2 of the Accelerator builds that inventory. Whether the inventory closes the finding is a determination for the Client's internal audit function under its own process. That process is Unknown.

**Incumbent management systems.** The Client already runs ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 management systems, so every artifact is designed to attach to them rather than stand alone. The specific attachment points in those systems are Unknown, because the Profile Block does not describe them. Examples include a risk methodology, document control, change control and nonconformity handling. The build team will identify the attachment points on Day 1. The names of the frameworks are not treated as evidence of any specific register, process, control or record.

## 3. The Five-Day Build Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

The spine respects two dependencies:

- The charter comes before the policies.
- The inventory comes before the risk register.

**Day 1: Governance charter and roles.** The build team drafts the AI governance charter. The charter covers purpose, scope, roles, decision rights and meeting cadence. Decision rights will include a step requiring German works council consultation before any AI activity touches production staff, as the stated constraint requires. Who carries out that consultation and when it occurs are Unknown and will be set by the Client. The charter is drafted to attach to the governance structures of the existing ISMS and quality management system, at attachment points the build team identifies. Board-layer oversight references AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). An executive checkpoint takes place on this day.

**Day 2: AI system inventory and classification.** The build team creates the inventory schema and populates it. The three known use cases are the first entries, recorded at the lifecycle stage the Profile Block states. Classification fields will include:

- Lifecycle stage.
- Operating jurisdiction.
- EU AI Act orientation category.
- Personal data processing relevant to GDPR.
- A customer data residency flag.
- A production staff touchpoint flag.

Values not established in the session are recorded as `Unknown`. EU AI Act classification is orientation only: confirm with external counsel. The team also runs a structured discovery exercise to surface AI systems not yet known.

**Day 3: Risk and impact assessment plus risk register.** Building on the Day 2 inventory, the team drafts a risk and impact assessment method and a risk register. The method is designed to align with the ISMS risk methodology, if the Client confirms that such a methodology exists. That alignment point is currently Unknown. The register is seeded with risk statements grounded in the three use cases and the June 2026 audit finding. Every seeded statement is labeled as a draft for Client validation.

**Day 4: Core policies and operating procedures.** Building on the Day 1 charter, the team drafts the policy and procedure set:

- Acceptable use.
- Lifecycle governance.
- Vendor and supplier governance.
- Incident response.
- Change management.

Each document is designed to attach to the corresponding ISMS or quality management system process, where the Client confirms one exists. The stated EU customer data constraint is written into vendor and supplier governance as a requirement. Provisions with legal effect under the EU AI Act or GDPR are orientation: confirm with external counsel.

**Day 5: Evidence model, implementation priorities and executive readout.** The team maps each artifact to the assurance question it answers. The team also builds a prioritized implementation plan. This plan sequences the work needed before visual inspection moves into production, along with the readiness steps for ISO/IEC 42001. The week closes with an executive readout and checkpoint.

The working method draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). It is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 4. Artifacts the Client Owns at Close

All artifacts are delivered in editable form and belong to the Client. At close, each artifact will carry a status of draft or reviewed. Adoption takes place through the Client's own approval process. Named owners for each artifact are Unknown until the Client assigns them on Day 1.

1. AI Governance Charter
2. Roles and Decision Rights Matrix
3. AI System Inventory and Classification Schema, with the three known use cases entered
4. AI Risk and Impact Assessment Method
5. AI Risk Register, with seeded draft risk statements for Client validation
6. AI Acceptable Use Policy
7. AI Lifecycle Governance Policy
8. AI Vendor and Supplier Governance Policy
9. AI Incident Response Procedure
10. AI Change Management Procedure
11. Regulatory Orientation Map for the EU AI Act and GDPR (orientation only: confirm with external counsel)
12. Evidence Model and Evidence Index
13. Prioritized Implementation Plan
14. Executive Readout Pack

## 5. Team Composition Asked of the Client

We ask the Client to designate a build team covering the following roles for all five days:

- General Counsel
- CISO
- Head of Quality
- Head of Data
- German plant manager
- Two internal auditors

We also ask the Client to name the executives who will attend the checkpoints on Days 1 and 5. Those attendees are currently Unknown.

## 6. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** five consecutive working days of live virtual working sessions with structured build time.
- **Dates:** Unknown, to be agreed.
- **Data handling:** the sessions work from system descriptions and process documentation. They do not require access to customer data records, which keeps the work consistent with the stated constraint that customer data must stay in the EU.
- **Price:** US$25,000.

The stated budget approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year covers this amount. The fiscal year boundaries are Unknown.

## 7. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To prepare for that date, we propose a short working call to confirm three things:

- The build team designations.
- The executive checkpoint attendees.
- A candidate week for the Accelerator.

We would also like to confirm whether ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 documentation can be shared before Day 1. Sharing it in advance would let the team identify attachment points from the first session.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
